Senses.Explanation: A lineage heir is the person selected or recognized to continue a teaching line; Chan lamp records make this person-label a principal genealogical heading. Qianyan Yuanzhang gives the corpus's clearest selection account: from among thousands, one is picked out to make the transmission and seed the lineage, “like lamp lighting lamp, like water joining water,” and therefore there is the designation “lineage heir.” Other records count sixteen heirs of Shoushan Xingnian or one collateral heir of Daoxin, while Prajnatara recognizes Bodhidharma and Michaka predicts an heir. Tang Shiji says that only twelve people were called Miyun Yuanwu's heirs, Shunzhi Emperor asks whose heir Wunian was, and an unnamed questioner asks why Baiyun Haihui did not select one. Chuiwan Guangzhen likewise cites Muzhou's having none rather than accepting indiscriminate succession. The role is not limited to ordained monks: one catalogue names a lay successor of a lay predecessor. Across 10,572 occurrences in 168 allowlisted texts, the term is a recurrent device for making Chan genealogy public, but a lineage heading does not assign every later exchange to the person named in that heading.

Senses.Note: The recurrent question “from whom did you obtain lineage succession?” (得法嗣何人) must not be paraphrased globally as “obtain lineage heirs.” The related verbal construction is “inherit the lineage from X” (嗣法於X) in its own entry.

Senses.Explanation: The succession relation or lineage affiliation itself, rather than the person who is an heir. Catalogues append people “whose lineage succession is not detailed” (未詳法嗣者); an unnamed questioner asks from whom Shexian Guisheng obtained lineage succession (師今得法嗣何人); and the messenger Wenxiang carries a written succession document (法嗣書) to Wuzu Fayan. The relation is not accepted merely because a later genealogy records it: Dahui Zonggao recounts Gaoting Jian's later succession to Deshan Xuanjian, then says that if Gaoting is to succeed Deshan, it is “not yet acceptable” because he is still separated from Deshan by the river. A single “lineage heir” gloss cannot describe an unknown affiliation, a succession document, or the predication “succeed Deshan” without changing the referent.
